turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
The README already points to `internal/mapengine/`. Let me verify with the actual source.Found the routing logic in `types.go` (`Map`, `mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`). Let me read those functions in full, plus check how the language/extension is detected.## Structural map engine implementation

**Package:** `internal/mapengine/` — four files, each implementing the `Mapper` interface (`Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error)`, defined in `internal/mapengine/types.go:47`):

| File | Symbol | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/mapengine/goast.go` | `GoASTMapper` (`goast.go:11,13`) | Parses Go via `go/ast` + `go/token`; walks top-level `GenDecl`/`FuncDecl` nodes (`goASTSymbols`, `goGenDeclSymbols`, `goFuncDeclSymbol`) |
| `internal/mapengine/treesitter.go` | `TreeSitterMapper` (`treesitter.go:12,25`) | Uses `gotreesitter` + a `grammars` package for TS/JS/Python/Rust; detects language via `grammars.DetectLanguage(path)` (`treesitter.go:93`), then looks up a `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` per language name to build a tagger/query and extract symbols with parent references (`computeTreeSitterParents`) |
| `internal/mapengine/regex.go` | `RegexMapper` (`regex.go:10,82`) | Line-pattern fallback; `rulesForPath` picks a rule set keyed by file extension (`regex.go:105`) |
| `internal/mapengine/types.go` | `Map`, `mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback` | Shared `Options`/`Result`/`Symbol` types and the engine-selection/dispatch logic |

## Engine selection per file

Dispatch happens in `internal/mapengine/types.go:125` (`Map`), based on `opts.Engine` (`auto` / `regex` / `tree-sitter` — normalized by `normalizeEngine`, `types.go:80`):

- `EngineRegex` → forces `RegexMapper` directly.
- `EngineTreeSitter` → forces `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=true)`, which still falls back to `RegexMapper` if tree-sitter errors (`types.go:160-172`).
- `EngineAuto` (default) → `mapAuto` (`types.go:143`), which switches on `filepath.Ext(path)`:
  - `.go` → `GoASTMapper`; on error, falls back to `RegexMapper` (marks `Fallback: true`).
  - `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=false)`, i.e. tree-sitter with silent regex fallback.
  - anything else → `RegexMapper` directly.
- Within tree-sitter itself, per-language routing is a second layer: `TreeSitterMapper.treeSitterEntry` (`treesitter.go:89`) calls `grammars.DetectLanguage(path)` to identify the language, then confirms a `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` exists for it via `languageConfigs()` (`treesitter.go:121`, backed by `defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()`), else fails and the outer fallback in `types.go` kicks in.

**CLI wiring:** the engine is user-selectable via `--map-engine auto|regex|tree-sitter` flag, registered in `internal/cli/ghx.go:211` and read at `ghx.go:112`, passed into `ghxlib.ReadOpts.MapEngine`, then into `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: mapengine.Engine(opts.MapEngine), ...})` in `internal/ghx/read.go:187-191`.

## Not verified
- I did not inspect the `grammars` package source itself (where `DetectLanguage` and `LangEntry`/`TokenSourceFactory` are defined) — likely a separate internal or vendored package, not shown in the `internal/mapengine` tree listing, so I can't confirm exactly how extension→grammar mapping is implemented there.
- I did not read `defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()` or `defaultRegexRules`/`regexRules` map contents in full detail beyond the map signatures shown.
- I did not check `internal/ghx/read.go` beyond the `--map` branch (e.g., glob expansion interaction with `--map`).

README:
# ghx — GitHub Code Exploration for AI Agents

One command does what takes 3-5 API calls. Batch file reads, code maps, search — all via `gh` CLI. Write JS programs that compose operations in one round-trip.

## Why

An agent wants to understand `packages/shadcn/src/utils/` in [shadcn-ui/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui):

**With `gh` CLI** — 4 turns, 4 API calls, reads 3 full files (3,761 tokens), sees 3 of 34 files:
```
gh api /repos/shadcn-ui/ui/contents/packages/shadcn/src/utils       → JSON with shas, urls, links (480 tokens for a file list)
gh api /repos/.../get-config.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (1,981 tokens — agent only needed exports)
gh api /repos/.../registries.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (676 tokens)
gh api /repos/.../frameworks.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (624 tokens)
```

**With ghx** — 2 turns, 2 API calls, maps 10 files (3,058 tokens), sees signatures of all 10:
```
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui packages/shadcn/src/utils                     → directory listing (199 tokens)
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui "packages/shadcn/src/utils/*.ts" --map        → signatures of 10 files (2,859 tokens)
```

Same token budget. The `gh` agent read 3 full files. The ghx agent saw the structure of 10 — imports, exports, function signatures — and knows which ones to drill into. Pass a file, get content. Pass a directory, get a listing. Pass a glob, get matching files. Same command, always useful output.
